Quantitative benchmarking and standardized safety evaluation are essential for advancing these systems toward predictable and clinically translatable therapeutic platforms.

title: Artificial Regulatory T Cells Orchestrate Phase‐Spanning Regeneration in Refractory Tissue Injuries
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Regulatory T cells (Tregs) possess potent multiphasic reparative capacity; however, their application is limited by ethical and regulatory challenges associated with live cell therapies. Treg‐derived exosomes (TExo) exhibit low immunogenicity while enriching regenerative signaling relative to parental Tregs. Current exosome carriers place greater emphasis on sustained release than on factors affecting vesicle stability, such as nonspecific interactions and confinement effects. Inspired by the multivesicular body (MVB), we engineered artificial Tregs (ATregs) with an MVB‐like architecture that integrates vesicle protection with sustained release through a reconstructed storage microenvironment. This design enables phase‐aligned TExo release and extends functional activity by more than an order of magnitude compared with free TExo. ATregs sequentially coordinate the suppression of inflammation, enhancement of angiogenesis, and stimulation of skin appendage regeneration. In diabetic wounds and deep second‐degree burn models, which represent intrinsic repair dysfunction and severe structural tissue loss, ATregs markedly accelerate healing and outperform conventional strategies across murine and porcine models. These findings overcome the key limitations of exosome therapies and open a new avenue for next‐generation regenerative therapeutics.

title: Biomaterial‐Based Controlled Release Systems for Spinal Cord Remyelination
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Spinal cord injury (SCI) triggers a complex secondary injury cascade characterized by oligodendrocyte (OL) death and axonal demyelination, leading to permanent neurological deficits. Despite the presence of endogenous oligodendrocyte progenitor cells (OPCs), the inhibitory microenvironment—marked by inflammation, glial scarring, and biochemical barriers—prevents effective remyelination. Traditional pharmacological treatments are further hindered by the blood‐spinal cord barrier and rapid clearance of intrathecal injections. This review examines the evolution of controlled release systems engineered to modulate the oligodendroglial lineage. We analyze macro‐ and micro‐scale platforms, including scaffolds, which provide mechanical and topographical cues to direct the fate of OLs and OPCs. Furthermore, we discuss advanced nanoscale vectors, such as nanoparticles and exosomes, designed to deliver high‐value payloads—including small molecules and therapeutic oligonucleotides—directly to the lesion site while minimizing systemic toxicity. Finally, we address critical translational gaps to bridge the divide between preclinical innovation and clinical application in restoring neural connectivity.

title: Vacancy‐Associated La–Ir Pairs Enable Water‐Derived Oxygen‐Hydroxyl Coupling for Durable Low‐Ir PEM Water Electrolysis
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Developing highly stable, low‐iridium catalysts is critical for acidic oxygen evolution, but is limited by structural degradation driven by acid corrosion and voltage polarization. Herein, we report an iridium and lanthanum co‐doped manganese‐cobalt spinel catalyst, Ir,La‐MCO δ , featuring octahedral La–Ir pairs (La oct –Ir oct ) with a theoretical favorable configuration of adjacent bridging and Ir z ‐axis oxygen vacancies. This low‐Ir catalyst Ir,La‐MCO δ (0.12 mg Ir cm −2 ) exhibits an overpotential of merely 220 mV at 10 mA cm −2 in pH = 1 electrolyte, and demonstrates robust operation for over 1550 h at 1 A cm −2 in a proton exchange membrane (PEM) water electrolyzer. Coupled (quasi)in situ characterizations and operando spectroscopy reveal that the adjacent oxygen vacancies mediate the evolution of oxygen intermediates, enabling water‐derived oxygen‐hydroxyl coupling with negligible lattice oxygen involvement, via a decoupled proton–electron transfer pathway. This mechanism preserves the structural integrity of the catalyst and yields a calculated reaction free‐energy change of merely 0.38 eV ( U = 1.23 V) for the most unfavorable oxygen‐hydroxyl coupling elementary step, thereby endowing Ir,La‐MCO δ with exceptional durability. This work provides a valuable mechanistic insight into designing highly stable defective catalysts.

title: Persistent Mn3+ Sites on Reduced MnO Enable Efficient Syngas Conversion
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Mn‐based materials are widely used for syngas conversion, where MnO is generally regarded as the catalytically active phase under reducing conditions. Yet catalysts derived from different Mn oxide precursors often exhibit markedly different performances despite evolving into the same MnO bulk structure during reaction. Here we show that trace Mn 3+ sites stabilized on oxygen‐deficient MnO surfaces serve as the decisive active sites. Time‐resolved energy‐dispersive x‐ray absorption spectroscopy combined with iterative target transformation factor analysis and depth‐resolved synchrotron photoemission spectroscopy reveals a persistent minor Mn 3 O 4 ‐like spectral contribution and its enrichment near the surface of Mn 2 O 3 ‐derived MnO. These stabilized sites strongly enhance CO adsorption and activation, thereby promoting C─O bond cleavage and markedly improving activity and selectivity for syngas‐to‐light‐olefin conversion. More broadly, this work reveals how minority surface sites can govern catalytic function despite identical bulk phases and establishes an operando strategy for quantitatively resolving low‐coverage active sites in reducible oxide catalysts.

title: Stabilizing Functional Nucleic Acids for Real‐Sample Diagnostics
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Functional nucleic acids (FNAs), including aptamers and DNAzymes, offer programmable recognition and catalysis for biosensing, but their performance in real samples is often compromised by nuclease degradation, matrix effects, and interface‐associated losses. For diagnostic translation, stability must, therefore, be defined not only as strand persistence, but as retained folding, binding, catalysis, and signal generation under assay‐relevant conditions. This review examines strategies for stabilizing FNAs in complex biological matrices and organizes the field around four design levers: Chemical, topological, architectural, and microenvironment/interface engineering. Chemical modification of sugars, backbones, and bases can reduce nuclease susceptibility, but requires functional validation. Topological approaches, including terminus shielding, circularization, covalent locking, and mechanically interlocked structures, limit strand accessibility, and reinforce functional conformations. Architectural strategies use multivalency, scaffolded presentation, DNA nanostructures, and rolling circle amplification‐derived concatemers to improve robustness and signal retention. Microenvironment engineering further stabilizes FNAs through controlled immobilization, antifouling interfaces, nanomaterial‐assisted protection, hydrogel or microgel confinement, and sample processing. Case studies in saliva, serum, urine, and stool illustrate how these levers can be combined to enable reliable FNA‐based real‐sample diagnostics.

title: Topological Engineering of NIR‐II Emissive Conjugated Oligomers With Unexpected Excited‐State Manifolds for Efficient Phototheranostics and Cancer Immunotherapy
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Phototheranostic agents operating in the second near‐infrared (NIR‐II) window hold great potential for precision cancer therapy, yet the rational regulation of excited‐state processes to simultaneously optimize fluorescence and phototherapeutic performances remains a fundamental challenge. Herein, we report a topology‐driven excited‐state engineering strategy for constructing conjugated oligomers with tailored excited‐state manifolds and multi‐channel excitation dynamics. By precisely manipulating molecular topology, conjugated topological oligomers achieve enhanced light‐harvesting capability and optimized exciton utilization, thereby enabling synergistic regulation of excitation dynamics. Under 808 nm laser irradiation, nanoparticles (NPs) derived from TBT‐3 exhibit 2.8‐fold enhanced NIR‐II fluorescence brightness, 2.7‐fold improved photothermal performance, and 7.5‐fold increased total reactive oxygen species (ROS) generation compared with TBT‐1. In vivo studies demonstrate that TBT‐3 NPs enable high‐resolution NIR‐II fluorescence imaging and efficient tumor elimination. Moreover, TBT‐3‐mediated phototherapy induces immunogenic cell death and enhances antitumor immunity, leading to improved therapeutic efficacy when combined with anti‐PD‐1 immune checkpoint blockade. This work provides a molecular topology‐based strategy for manipulating excited‐state landscapes and establishes conjugated oligomers as versatile candidates for NIR‐II phototheranostics and cancer immunotherapy.

title: Overcoming the Spin Barrier of Oxygen Redox Chemistry in Lithium–Oxygen Batteries via Metal–Support Magnetic Interaction
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT A major bottleneck for the practical application of lithium–oxygen (Li–O 2 ) batteries is the high overpotential resulting from sluggish kinetics of oxygen redox chemistry. This kinetic limitation can rise in part from the spin‐state transition barriers in converting triplet oxygen ( 3 O 2 ) into peroxide species, alongside the parasitic generation of singlet oxygen ( 1 O 2 ). Here, we demonstrate that metal–support magnetic interactions can effectively overcome this spin barrier. Using palladium (Pd) nanoparticles anchored on ferrimagnetic CoFe 2 O 4 (CFO) substrates as a model catalyst, we reveal that interfacial magnetic coupling restructures the spin and electronic states of Pd sites, generating spin‐polarized active ensembles with optimized adsorption toward oxygen intermediates. This interfacial spin‐electronic effect promotes the conversion of 3 O 2 into peroxide species while suppressing parasitic 1 O 2 evolution during charging, thereby improving the reversibility of oxygen redox chemistry. As a result, the Pd/CFO catalyst achieves a low charging overpotential of 0.05 V and remarkable energy efficiency (91.2%) under spin alignment. This finding establishes metal–support magnetic interaction as a powerful strategy for controlling spin‐dependent oxygen electrocatalysis, providing a general design principle for catalysts involving multi‐site interactions.

title: Biomarker and Bioorthogonality Dual‐Locked Chemiluminescent Probes for Cancer Urine Test
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Bioorthogonality‐activatable optical imaging activates caged or quenched probes via bioorthogonal reactions for disease diagnosis. Although chemiluminescence enables low‐background detection, it has rarely been applied to bioorthogonality‐activatable imaging. Here, we synthesize chemiluminescent tetrazine probes (CLTZs) by coupling a tetrazine acceptor to a phenoxy‐1,2‐dioxetane donor through π‐conjugated vinylene linkers, enabling biomarker and bioorthogonality dual‐locked activation for cancer urine testing. Unlike conventional chemiluminophores, tetrazine in CLTZs mediates an internal‐conversion‐to‐a‐dark‐state quenching mechanism, suppressing chemiluminescence even after phenolate formation. Strong chemiluminescence is restored only when the phenolate form undergoes bioorthogonal reaction with bicyclononyne (BCN), generating pyridazine‐containing donor–π–acceptor chemiluminophores. This unique dark state enables development of an H 2 O 2 and bioorthogonality dual‐locked probe ( H BCP), emitting only when both H 2 O 2 and BCN are present. By engineering BCN into a cancer‐activatable bioorthogonal urinary reporter ( C BUR) that releases renal‐clearable BCN in tumors, a chemiluminescent bioorthogonal pair ( H BCP & C BUR) is created. This pair achieves in vivo tumor imaging with a signal‐to‐background ratio of 438 and detects lung metastasis in early urinary assays with up to 23.9‐fold signal enhancement over healthy mice. This work provides a molecular design for bioorthogonality‐activatable chemiluminescence toward noninvasive, sensitive disease diagnosis.

title: Controlled Hydrogen Delivery by Single‐Atom Ru Accelerates Electrocatalytic Ammonia Synthesis
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Electrocatalytic nitric oxide reduction to ammonia (NORR) offers a dual opportunity for NO remediation and decentralized NH 3 production, yet its efficiency is often limited by competing pathways and unclear structure–function relationships. Here we introduce a reactant‐shunting strategy that installs a guiding electrocatalytic step via isolated Ru atoms to supply surface‐bound * H species and enforce a Langmuir–Hinshelwood (LH) hydrogenation pathway. Using Ru 1 /Co 3 O 4 as a model catalyst, we show that single Ru sites promote water adsorption and dissociation, forming stable Ru‐H intermediates that thermodynamically and kinetically accelerate the coupling‐hydrogenation steps in NORR. The optimized catalyst delivers an NH 3 yield of 533.49 µmol cm −2 h −1 with a 97.19% faradaic efficiency, surpassing state‐of‐the‐art systems. The reactant‐shunting principle further generalizes across multiple oxide hosts, enhancing NH 3 productivity by up to threefold. These findings establish pathway steering through controlled hydrogen delivery as a powerful strategy for high‐efficiency electrocatalytic ammonia synthesis.

title: Modular Construction of Cyclic and Linear Quaternary Carbon Centers through Visible‐Light‐Induced Triplet Nitrene Transfer Reaction
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT All‐carbon quaternary centers represent a fundamental structural unit found in a wide range of functional molecules. Within the versatile synthetic toolbox, the semipinacol rearrangement (SPR) stands as one of the most powerful tools for assembling this sterically congested motif. In this context, ‌radical‐mediated SPR pathways‌, especially those entailing alkyl migrations, remain underexplored from a strategic standpoint. Herein, we report a visible light‐promoted formal SPR of tertiary allyl alcohols using in situ‐generated triplet nitrene species as the initiator under redox‐neutral conditions. This method demonstrates broad substrate scope, enabling efficient construction of all‐carbon quaternary centers across various steric environments, including rigid cyclic/spiro frameworks and flexible acyclic systems. Mechanistic investigations reveal substrate‐dependent pathways: alkenyl cyclobutanols undergo triplet nitrene addition followed by concurrent ring‐expansion and hydrogen atom transfer (HAT) to form cyclic ketones, while nonactivated allyl alcohols proceed through aziridination/ring‐opening/SPR sequences to produce linear β‐amino ketones. Preliminary biological assessments of these α‐quaternary β‐aminoketone derivatives revealed that compound 4a exhibited potent anti‐DENV‐2 activity, with an EC 50 value of 0.95 ± 0.02 µM against viral replication.

title: In Situ and Operando Techniques for Electrocatalysis in Renewable Energy Applications
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Electrocatalysis is essential for renewable energy conversion, yet the mechanisms governing catalytic performance remain poorly understood due to the complex nature of electrochemical interfaces. Advances in nanomaterial synthesis and high‐resolution characterization now allow detailed structural and compositional analysis, but static methods fall short of capturing the dynamic behaviors of active sites during operation. In this review, we focus on the growing role of in situ and operando techniques such as optical, X‐ray, and electron‐based, in resolving catalytic structure and reactivity under real‐life working conditions. These methods offer unparalleled access to the evolution of surface species, reaction intermediates, and interfacial topologies that govern catalytic functions. We highlight how in situ and operando studies have revealed transient phenomena and mechanistic details previously inaccessible, and discuss their critical roles in advancing systems for water splitting, CO 2 /N 2 reduction, and fuel cells related renewable energy applications. Beyond highlighting the real‐time transformations captured by operando and in situ methods, this review underscores how coupling operando datasets with theoretical modeling and machine learning can accelerate mechanistic discovery and enable rational catalyst design. By extracting hidden correlations and guiding closed‐loop experimentation, data‐driven approaches promise to reduce reliance on empirical trial‐and‐error and unlock predictive control over catalytic performance. Taken together, these developments position operando characterization, when coupled with AI‐driven interpretation, as a cornerstone of future energy research, providing a pathway to accelerate discovery, design, and deployment of next‐generation electrocatalysts.

title: RNA Organelles in DNA‐Based Artificial Cells Provide Spatial Aptamer Functions and Enhanced Signal Processing
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Naturally occurring biomolecular condensates orchestrate key cellular processes by creating spatially distinct reaction environments, yet engineering synthetic condensates that combine structural programmability with spatioselectively encoded function remains challenging. Here, we report multiphase DNA–RNA artificial cells (ACs) that embed functional RNA condensates as organelle‐like compartments within programmable DNA core–shell ACs. A single thermal assembly protocol yields three‐phase ACs comprising a glassy RNA core organelle embedded in a liquid‐like DNA compartment, surrounded by a crosslinked DNA shell. The RNA organelles contain aptamer function, enabling selective protein recruitment and small‐molecule activation, while the DNA scaffold provides independent addressability, modulates RNA‐condensate size, and enhances resistance to serum‐mediated degradation. We further show that RNA chemistry can be used to adjust environmental responsiveness: unmodified RNA organelles undergo rapid degradation in serum and release captured protein cargo, whereas 2′‐fluoro‐modified RNA organelles remain stable for at least 24 h. Finally, by coupling transcriptional modules localized in the DNA core to cell‐free protein translation in the surrounding medium, we establish sender–receiver communication between AC populations and self‐actuating signal processing within individual DNA–RNA ACs. These results establish hybrid nucleic‐acid ACs as programmable, spatially organized systems that couple compartment architecture, RNA molecular recognition, and biochemical communication.

title: Double Reduction of Ph3B to a Dianionic Borane With a Powerful SrI Intermediate
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Reduction of [(BDI)SrI] 2 with KC 8 generated in situ a (BDI)Sr I species which enabled the reduction of Ph 3 B to the Ph 3 B 2− dianion (BDI = HC[(Me)C═N‐DIPeP] 2 , DIPeP = 2,6‐(Et 2 CH) 2 ‐phenyl). The product (BDI)Sr(BPh 3 )Sr(BDI) features a Ph 3 B 2− dianion that is bridging two Sr 2+ cations by interaction with one of the Ph rings. This polarizes a large part of the electron density in the bridging Ph ring (NPA charge: −1.53) whereas the B is slightly positive (+0.44). The HOMO of the complex mainly consists of the π*‐orbital in the bridging Ph ring overlapping with Sr d ‐orbitals. However, there is also 18% contribution of the B p ‐orbital. In solution, there is coalescence of 1 H NMR signals of all three Ph rings. Complex (BDI)Sr(BPh 3 )Sr(BDI) can react as a 2 e transfer reagent or as a B‐nucleophile. It reacts with I 2 to Ph 3 B and [(BDI)SrI] 2 . Reaction with Ph 3 B led to formation of a Gomberg‐type dimer. The reaction with PhI is smooth and selectively gave (BDI)Sr(Ph 4 B) and [(BDI)SrI] 2 , likely through direct nucleophilic attack of an electron rich B atom at PhI. Isolation of a complex with the elusive Ph 3 B 2− dianion demonstrates the very high reducing power of in situ generated (BDI)Sr I species.

title: Structural Softness–Rigidity Mediation Enables Multicolor Emission and Long‐Lived Phosphorescence in Hf/Zr Halides
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Multicolor fluorescence, typically favored by soft environments, and phosphorescence, which relies on rigid lattices to stabilize triplet excitons, are fundamentally incompatible and hard to coexist within a single material. Here, we report a crown–ether–directed lattice assembly that integrates [HfCl 6 ] 2‒ /[ZrCl 6 ] 2‒ octahedra and DB18C6@M(K + /Rb + ) supramolecular, yielding four unknown organic–inorganic hybrid Hf/Zr halides. Notably, (DB18C6@K) 2 (CH 3 CN) 2 HfCl 6 achieves an exceptional room‐temperature phosphorescence (RTP) quantum yield (Φ p ) of 54.43%, a long lifetime of 0.8 s, and a visually discernible afterglow persisting up to 6 s. Moreover, these materials exhibit excitation–dependent multicolor emission, producing green and blue–white outputs under 302 and 365 nm irradiation, respectively. This unique multimodal luminescence originates from the synergistic interplay between the balanced soft‐rigid lattice provided by the crown‐ether framework and heavy – atom Hf/Zr centers, which facilitates intersystem crossing, enabling both efficient RTP and tunable multichannel pathways. It has been confirmed by the high–pressure synchrotron angle–dispersive x–ray diffraction and Raman results. Overall, this work establishes a heavy–atom–based structural mediation which may offer a generalizable route to high‐efficiency, multichannel, and stimuli‐responsive RTP materials.

title: In situ reduction-driven formation of sub-nanometer alternating heterostructures
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Sub-nanometer alternating heterostructures provide a platform for modulating electronic structure and interfacial reactivity through strong atom-level coupling, with potential applications in energy conversion. However, their precise construction remains challenging. Here we show a strategy for constructing sub-nanometer alternating heterostructures through confined spinodal decomposition and ligand-mediated in situ reduction. Oleylamine ligands adsorbed on NiMoO4 sub-nanowires act as mild reductants, selectively reducing Ni2+ to spatially confined metallic Ni domains and forming coherent Ni/NiMoO4 heterointerfaces. Experimental and theoretical analyses suggest that the Ni/NiMoO4 interfaces modify the local electronic structure and facilitate the adsorption and activation of hydrogen evolution intermediates. The resulting catalyst requires an overpotential of 14.4 ± 2.9 mV to reach 10 mA cm−2 in 1 M KOH and delivers 2 A cm−2 at 1.62 V in an anion-exchange membrane electrolyzer at 80 oC, with stable operation over 2200 h at 25 °C. These findings provide insights into the construction and interfacial regulation of sub-nanometer heterostructures through in situ reduction.

title: HCV incidence and prevalence trends among people who use drugs in France 2004 to 2023
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Hepatitis C virus (HCV) remains a key public health challenge, particularly among people who use and inject drugs (PWUD, PWID). While direct-acting antivirals (DAA) have revolutionized HCV treatment, meeting the WHO’s 2030 elimination target requires accurate estimation of incidence and prevalence to guide prevention and care. We analyze cross-sectional surveys conducted in France in 2004, 2013, and 2023, recruiting PWUD at harm reduction services and collecting behavioral and biological data. We estimate age-and time-dependent prevalence of HCV antibodies and HCV RNA using multivariate regression models while incidence was estimated from two-state transmission models. The demographic profile of PWUD has aged over time (mean age 35 years in 2004 vs. 44 in 2023) while injection prevalence remained stable (61.7% in 2023). Between 2013 and 2023, HCV burden declined substantially: HCV RNA prevalence fell from 19.4% (95% CI 16.3–23.0) to 9.5% (7.2–12.3) among all PWUD, and from 29.6% to 14.5% among PWID. Incidence among PWID decreased from 6.5 (4.1–8.0) to 2.4 (1.4–4.2) per 100 person-years. These reductions likely reflect the combined impact of DAA scale-up and harm reduction policies, marking substantial progress toward elimination targets. However, ongoing transmission highlights persistent barriers requiring targeted public health actions.

title: Time-lapse RESOLFT nanoscopy empowered by deep learning
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Capturing the dynamic interplay of proteins and organelles within cells requires microscopy methods with high spatial and temporal resolution. Reversible Saturable OpticaL Fluorescent Transition (RESOLFT) demonstrated great potential for live cell nanoscopy by using patterned light and reversibly switching fluorescent probes. Despite the latest improvement in both switching probes and optical schemes, the duration and frame rate of the time-lapse are still limited by photobleaching and spatial sampling steps. Here, we present two distinct strategies based on deep learning to restore low signal-to-noise-ratio (SNR) or under-sampled images pushing the experimental boundaries of RESOLFT. We demonstrate the capability of Hierarchical DivNoising (HDN) to restore low-SNR RESOLFT data while maintaining full spatial resolution, both in supervised and unsupervised settings. This allows a 10-fold reduction of light dose per frame, and up to 5 times longer imaging. Then, we present Fast-MoNaLISA, a method that reduces the acquisition time of any point-scanning systems. This allows a 4-fold increase in frame rate, and a reduction of scanning artefacts. Overall, our methods open up possibilities for dynamic data acquisition at the sub-organelle level, such as vesicles budding in and out from intact mitochondria, or the actin meshwork formation and dissociation.

title: Energy transition under fragmentation: A threshold analysis of inclusive governance in developing economies
abstract: Although institutional quality is widely recognised as important for environmental performance, less is known about whether the governance–energy relationship varies across levels of institutional capacity. This study examines the relationship between inclusive governance, energy intensity, and CO 2 emissions volatility across 71 developing economies in the context of an increasingly fragmented global energy system. We focus on whether the governance–energy relationship varies across levels of institutional capacity. Inclusive governance is measured using a composite index incorporating political institutional quality, gender representation, and income equality. The empirical analysis uses a piecewise panel specification based on the sample median of inclusive governance, with system-GMM and local-projection estimates providing supplementary sensitivity evidence. Inclusive governance is negatively and significantly associated with energy intensity in both governance regimes in the baseline specification, with a somewhat stronger association in the higher-governance regime. However, this nonlinear pattern is sensitive to alternative estimators and breakpoints and is therefore interpreted as suggestive rather than definitive. In contrast, inclusive governance is not significantly associated with CO 2 emissions volatility across most specifications. These findings indicate that the relationship between governance and environmental performance may be outcome-specific: institutional capacity is more clearly associated with energy efficiency than with emissions volatility. The results are interpreted as conditional associations rather than causal effects and suggest that the environmental relevance of governance may vary with both institutional capacity and the outcome being examined.

title: A method quantifying soil melanin to understand fungal impacts on soil carbon stability
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Fungal necromass, particularly dead microbial cells rich in melanin, is an important contributor to long-term soil carbon stabilization. Progress in understanding the role of soil melanin is limited by the lack of validated analytical methods. DNA-based approaches estimate only the genetic potential for melanin production and therefore provide indirect evidence of melanin occurrence. To directly assess soil melanin, we evaluated spectroscopic and spectrophotometric assays; however, both approaches proved insufficiently specific due to interference from chemically related compounds. Here, we introduce a liquid chromatography method that enables quantification of major fungal melanin types in soils. By enabling direct quantification of fungal melanin in soil, this framework allows longstanding hypotheses regarding melanized fungal necromass and soil carbon stabilization to be tested mechanistically. Here, we show with the proposed method that soil melanin concentrations are strongly correlated with total soil carbon, supporting a central role for fungal melanin in long-term soil carbon stabilization.

title: An IscS Persulfide Donates the Sulfur for Ribosomal Protein uL16 Thioamidation
abstract: ABSTRACT Posttranslational sulfur incorporation into peptide backbones is increasingly reported. These efforts broaden our understanding of thioamides, which have distinct conformational and hydrogen‐bonding properties compared with amides. YcaO‐catalyzed thioamidation of the ribosomal protein uL16 reportedly occurs across thousands of Pseudomonadota. Here, we identify the cysteine desulfurase IscS, a crucial component of iron–sulfur cluster assembly, as the direct sulfur donor for uL16 thioamidation. Genetic deletion, in vitro reconstitution, kinetic analysis, sulfide scavenging, and mutational studies support this conclusion. Our data support a mechanism in which the IscS persulfide attacks the O ‐phosphorylated uL16 backbone amide to form an IscS–uL16 disulfide intermediate. This labile disulfide is rapidly reduced, and the resulting hemiorthothioamide collapses with phosphate release to give the thioamide. IscS binds uL16 with mid‐nanomolar affinity and can be displaced by other IscS‐dependent sulfur acceptors. IscS promotes formation of the 2:2 YcaO–uL16 complex from the otherwise predominant 1:1 complex. Structural and mutational studies identify uL16 residues important for catalytically competent enzyme–substrate interactions. These findings define the sulfur delivery pathway for uL16 thioamidation and reveal an additional role of the IscS persulfide beyond iron–sulfur cluster assembly, suggesting it serves as another nucleophile for YcaO‐catalyzed backbone modification.

title: UV/X‐Ray‐Induced Reduction of Eu 3+ to Eu 2+ in Rare‐Earth‐Based Halide Double Perovskite for Material‐Discriminative X‐Ray Imaging
abstract: ABSTRACT Stacked scintillators for x‐ray energy discrimination require at least two emission bands with sufficient spectral separation to avoid signal crosstalk. Rare‐earth‐based double perovskites exhibit narrow‐band luminescence at multiple visible wavelengths, which is advantageous for such designs. However, an efficient narrow‐band blue emission has not yet been realized, hindering further development. Here, efficient Eu 2+ blue luminescence is achieved in Cs 2 (Li/Na/K)(Lu/Y/Gd)Cl 6 under ambient conditions via photo‐induced reduction of Eu 3+ to Eu 2+ , eliminating harsh reducing atmospheres. The reduction is driven by 254 nm UV or x‐ray irradiation, while mild heating and x‐ray‐induced lattice distortion assist carrier migration. The unique multi‐cation structure provides cation vacancies that trap holes, stabilizing the reduction. The resulting Eu 2+ emits narrow‐band blue light at 450 nm (FWHM 25 nm, PLQY 84.1%, 19 000 ph/MeV) in Cs 2 NaLuCl 6 , and coexisting Eu 3+ shows narrow‐band red emission, achieving a 144 nm spectral separation. Taking advantage of this well‐separated dual emission, a stacked scintillator device enables highly material‐discriminative x‐ray imaging.

title: Asymmetric bloom lengthening drives high-latitude ocean chlorophyll accumulation imbalance
source: Earth and environmental sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Terrestrial ecosystems maintain a stable time-allocation budget between growth and senescence, but whether this applies to the ocean remains unclear. Using fused satellite LiDAR and ocean-color data (2007–2022), we show that marine phenology is variable and asymmetric. In high latitudes ( > 50°N), the bloom growth-to-decline ratio (RGD) is declining by ~5.3% per decade. While the chlorophyll-increase phase has lengthened by 2.3–5.5 days, the post-peak chlorophyll-decline phase has extended disproportionately by 5.7–6.2 days. Environmental sensitivity analyses reveal distinct hemispheric patterns in the statistical associations between phenological variability and multiple co-varying physical and biogeochemical factors, consistent with contrasting nutrient regimes between the Northern and Southern high-latitude oceans. We further show that these shifts are associated with spatially heterogeneous changes in marine chlorophyll accumulation patterns. Our results identify bloom asymmetry as an important dimension of marine phenological change, providing an observational baseline for evaluating future links between chlorophyll phenology, ecosystem timing, and polar biogeochemical processes under climate change.

title: Intensification of near-inertial currents in the Atlantic Ocean over the past two decades
source: Earth and environmental sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Near-inertial currents (NICs) play a key role in surface material redistribution and ocean mixing, yet their long-term variability remains poorly known. Using in situ current measurements from surface drifters, we provide observational evidence for a pronounced intensification of surface NICs in the Atlantic Ocean over the past two decades (2003–2022). Basin–mean NIC strength increases at a rate of 3.8 ± 1.7% per decade, with a spatial pattern characterized by strengthening in the South Atlantic and the high-latitude North Atlantic, and weakening in the low-latitude North Atlantic. We further show that these trends in Atlantic NICs are primarily driven by changes in near-inertial wind forcing, particularly those associated with mesoscale weather systems, while variations in mixed-layer depth playing a minor role. This observed intensification of Atlantic NICs may have important implications for ocean transport and mixing, and needs to be properly represented in the current generation of climate models.

title: ETSAM: effectively segmenting cell membranes in cryo-electron tomograms
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Cryogenic Electron Tomography (cryo-ET) is an emerging experimental technique used to visualize cell structures and macromolecules in their native cellular environment. Accurate segmentation of cell structures in cryo-ET tomograms, such as cell membranes, supports the study of cellular organization and function. However, several inherent limitations in cryo-ET, including the very low signal-to-noise ratio, missing wedge artifacts from limited tilt angles, and other noise artifacts, collectively hinder the reliable identification and delineation of these structures. In this study, we present ETSAM, a two-stage Segment Anything Model 2 (SAM2)-based fine-tuned AI method that effectively segments cell membranes in tomograms. It is trained on a diverse dataset comprising 83 experimental tomograms from the CryoET Data Portal (CDP) database and 28 simulated tomograms generated using PolNet. On an independent test set of 17 experimental tomograms for which ground-truth annotations are available, ETSAM outperforms other deep learning based methods by robustly identifying cell membranes with high sensitivity while also maintaining better precision.

title: Energy policy and energy poverty under geopolitical fragmentation: Evidence on structural constraints
An automated operon refactoring workflow for heterologous expression of non-ribosomal peptide biosynthetic gene clusters
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Microbial genomes encode numerous biosynthetic gene clusters, yet most remain experimentally uncharacterized, particularly large non-ribosomal peptide synthetase (NRPS) clusters that resist conventional cloning. Existing refactoring approaches are labor-intensive, depend on de novo DNA synthesis and are difficult to scale. Here we show that OSAR (One-Step Assembly and Refactoring)—an automated platform integrating algorithmic primer design with yeast homologous-recombination cloning—directly assembles and refactors NRPS clusters without custom DNA synthesis. We apply OSAR to 34 low- to medium-GC bacterial NRPS clusters (7–78 kb) and successfully assemble 31. Expression in Bacillus subtilis yields 29 peptides from 10 clusters. Several products arose from cryptic biosynthetic behaviors such as potential module skipping and premature release. OSAR provides a practical workflow for assembly and refactoring of NRPS clusters and may facilitate the translation of sequence information into natural products.

title: A supergene and genomic mosaicism are associated with phenotypic evolution in Galápagos tree finches
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Adaptive radiations provide powerful models to study the origins of phenotypic novelty and species diversity. Darwin’s finches constitute a classic example of adaptive radiation, in which beak morphology is a key trait related to fitness. Here, we focus on Camarhynchus tree finches by analyzing whole genomes in combination with morphological data to revisit long-standing questions regarding their origins raised before genetic evidence became available. Camarhynchus diversified over the last 100,000 years, yielding some striking morphological differences despite shallow genetic divergence. We identify several highly differentiated loci, including G03, a supergene affecting beak and body size. We reveal a striking example of genomic mosaicism, in which autosomal differentiation between two sympatric species is restricted primarily to a single locus -(G03)- that approaches fixation, shifting them from one phenotypic optimum to another. Contextualized in a broader phylogenetic framework, we also reveal an unexpected diversity of G03 haplotypes and show that the small and large G03 alleles diverged early in the radiation, suggesting a key genetic innovation enabling ecological expansion among species of Darwin’s finches. Our results further establish Camarhynchus as a model example of speciation with gene flow, underscoring the broader role of hybridization in generating biodiversity.

title: Synergistic Regulation of High Dielectric Constant and H‐Aggregation for Efficient and Thickness‐Tolerant Organic Solar Cells
abstract: ABSTRACT While the power conversion efficiency (PCE) of organic solar cells (OSCs) has advanced rapidly, their sensitivity with respect to active layer thickness hinders industrial fabrication. Herein, a novel acceptor BMD‐6F was synthesized via molecular engineering of L8‐BO, which realizes synergistic optimization of dielectric constant (6.20, 1.5 × that of L8‐BO) and H‐aggregation and thus enriches charge transport pathways, facilitates exciton dissociation, and suppresses recombination. As a result, the PM6:L8‐BO:BMD‐6F ternary OSC delivered a champion PCE of 20.34% at 100 nm, and exhibited excellent thickness tolerance with PCEs of 18.23% (300 nm) and 16.18% (500 nm). This work establishes a design principle for high‐efficiency, thickness‐tolerant OSCs, promising industrial applications.

title: GlycoStamp-seq: Single-cell nascent sialoglycometabolomics captures sialylation dynamics in immune cells of an oxaliplatin-treated bladder cancer mouse model
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Dynamic remodeling of immune cell-surface glycans reflects cellular state and immune activity. Despite advances in single-cell glyco-profiling, current methods primarily capture pre-existing glycan epitopes, providing limited information on dynamic sialoglycans. Here, we present GlycoStamp-seq, a method to profile nascent sialoglycan dynamics by coupling Ac₄ManNAz-based metabolic glycoengineering with single-cell RNA/TCR sequencing (scRNA/TCR-seq) and scDyna-seq. We apply GlycoStamp-seq by injecting Ac₄ManNAz into oxaliplatin-treated mice with subcutaneous bladder tumors, days before extracting tumor-derived single-cell suspensions for sequencing. Following oxaliplatin treatment, a subset of CD8⁺ T cells in the tumor immune microenvironment exhibits elevated nascent sialoglycan activity, enhanced effector programs, and increased clonal expansion. Furthermore, elevated nascent sialoglycan levels mark antigen-reactive CD8⁺ T cells with increased anti-tumor efficacy in vitro and in vivo. GlycoStamp-seq may thus serve as a versatile platform for profiling nascent sialoglycan dynamics in complex tissues, thereby expanding the single-cell multi-omics toolkit and providing insights into sialoglycan dynamics during therapeutic response.

title: Wavelength-Selective Magneto-Optical Diodes Based on Rare-Earth Chiral Molecular Crystals
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Chiral materials, integrating structural breaking of mirror-symmetry, exhibit physical properties that cannot be observed in centrosymmetric analogues. Among these properties, optical magneto-chiral anisotropy, the nonreciprocal absorption of light shown by chiral magnetized systems, is emerging as an enabling technology in magneto-optics and photonics. Here, we report on enantiopure chiral molecular crystals based on the erbium(III) rare-earth ion that display nonreciprocal, wavelength-selective, magnetic field-induced variations of the optical absorption coefficients up to ca. 200% for the intrashell f–f electronic transition falling in the 1.5 μm telecom wavelength range. Such a response is associated with an exceptionally high Magneto-Chiral Dichroism induced by the strong spin–orbit coupling of the Er(III) and the helical chirality at the lanthanide center, exalted by the magnetic-dipole-allowed character of the electronic transition. This chirality-induced nonreciprocal magneto-optical response represents a proof of concept for the use of these chiral crystalline molecular materials as potential components in magneto-optical diodes.

title: Who leads the global gas market? Geopolitics and price transmission between the U.S. and Europe
Photonic Klein Tunnelling in Silicon Topological Materials for Terahertz 6G Interconnects
abstract: ABSTRACT Topological photonics enables robust light transport along engineered interfaces, but transport across a potential barrier placed within such an interface, and the range of barrier strengths over which it survives, remain largely unexplored. Here we experimentally demonstrate photonic Klein tunnelling in a Complementary Metal‐Oxide‐Semiconductor (CMOS) compatible silicon valley photonic crystal at terahertz frequencies. A local, inversion‐symmetric barrier is introduced into a valley kink channel, with its strength Δ controlled through the geometry of the triangular holes. The barrier strength is calibrated using the local Dirac‐frequency shift, establishing a direct relation between photonic crystal geometry and the effective tight‐binding potential. We find that transmission remains close to its barrier‐free value for Δ below the nearest‐neighbour hopping amplitude t , and is strongly suppressed as Δ approaches t . Momentum‐space analysis shows valley pseudospin preserved to better than 98% across two cascaded barriers. We further demonstrate Klein‐tunnelling transport through multibarrier, Ω‐shaped and power‐splitter devices, supporting terahertz data transmission at rates up to 100 Gbit s − 1 . Our findings underpin a new design framework for resilient and high‐capacity terahertz photonic integrated circuits.

title: Topochemical Engineering of Two‐Dimensional MXenes and Beyond
abstract: ABSTRACT Two‐dimensional (2D) materials have gained tremendous attention for their structural diversity and versatile functionality. However, conventional synthesis and post‐synthetic modification often provide limited control over where and how structural or chemical changes occur, restricting the precise tailoring of composition, atomic configuration, and electronic structure. Topochemical engineering offers a distinct approach by directing chemical reactions at predefined sites while preserving key structural features of parent materials, thereby enabling precise and selective modulation at the atomic and molecular levels through four core strategies: conversion, termination, substitution, and transformation. Herein, we present a systematic and critical review of the latest advances in the topochemical engineering of MXenes and other representative 2D materials (TE‐2DMs). We establish the conceptual framework and classification criteria for these strategies and discuss their implementation and underlying structural regulation mechanisms. Special emphasis is placed on the structure–performance correlations of TE‐2DMs in electrochemical energy storage and conversion. We further summarize general design principles and practical guidelines for selecting and implementing appropriate topochemical strategies. Finally, we identify key challenges and emerging opportunities in this rapidly evolving field, with the aim of guiding the rational design of high‐performance 2D functional materials for next‐generation electrochemical energy technologies.

title: Albumin Orchestrates Type‐I ROS Conversion for Efficient Intracellular Bacterial Clearance
abstract: ABSTRACT Type‐I photosensitization addresses the dilemma of intracellular bacterial hypoxia‐induced photodynamic therapeutic (PDT) inefficacy, yet precise targeting and eradicating sequestered pathogens remains a formidable challenge. Herein, we engineer an albumin‐based photodynamic conversion nanoparticles integrating target‐specific recognition with controlled antibacterial functions to precisely eliminate intracellular pathogens and restore infected cell activity. Mechanistic studies reveal a vertically‐crossed conformation that promotes intramolecular electron transfer and charge separation, redirecting photosensitizer (PS) reactivity toward type‐I reactive oxygen species (ROS) generation. Electron‐rich albumin further enhances cationic PS +• recycling, photostability, and O 2 −• production, while its selective cytoplasmic delivery via receptor/charge interactions enables preferential accumulation in intracellular bacteria, with reduced off‐target organelle engagement. We demonstrate application in S. aureus ‐infected sepsis showing high type‐I ROS levels for antibacterial function from the nanoparticles to restore redox and immune homeostasis without noticeable toxicity. This work pioneers a conformationally‐gated ROS conversion approach for eliminating intracellular bacterial infections, merging mechanistic precision with therapeutic potential for clinical sepsis management.

title: Sustained‐Release Regulation on FAPbI 3 Crystallization to Enhance Photo‐Thermal Stability of Perovskite Solar Cells
abstract: ABSTRACT Controlling crystallization kinetics of FAPbI 3 perovskite is crucial for improving crystal quality, device performance and stability. Herein, we report a sustained‐release strategy to regulate the PbI 2 ‐to‐FAPbI 3 conversion. PbI 2 lattice expansion arising from the interaction between PEI (oligomeric poly(ethyleneimine)) and iodide species suppresses nonuniform PbI 2 crystallization and facilitates FAI infiltration. Moreover, the weak interaction between oligomeric PEGDE (poly(ethylene glycol) diglycidyl ether) and FAI slows the reaction between FAI and PbI 2 , leading to homogeneous phase conversion during annealing. Consequently, enlarged FAPbI 3 grains are obtained with improved crystallographic orientation, reduced strain and suppressed nonradiative recombination. Furthermore, released PEI and PEGDE undergo in situ crosslinking to form a three‐dimensional network that passivates grain boundaries, stabilizes microstructure and affords inner encapsulation. The resulting champion n‐i‐p device presents a power conversion efficiency of 26.6% (certified 26.17%). Both films and devices exhibit enhanced photothermal stability. The PEI/PEGDE‐treated device maintains 92% of its initial efficiency at 85 °C for over 1,100 h, 96% after continuous illumination (∼100 mW cm − 2 ) and maximum‐power‐point (MPP) tracking for over 1,500 h, and 89% after MPP tracking at 85 °C over 12 days. This work offers a polymerization‐assisted route for synchronizing crystallization control, defect passivation and inner encapsulation to enhance perovskite solar‐cell stability.

title: Beyond nature: charting the roadmap to intelligent biomanufacturing for sustainable biohydrogen
abstract: Hydrogen has been recognized as a key pillar of future energy systems in the global pursuit of carbon neutrality. However, hydrogen production processes still highly rely on fossil fuels. Biohydrogen production is a microbial-based process that converts biomass, organic waste, and solar energy into hydrogen via dark fermentation, photo-fermentation, or photolytic water-splitting pathways. It is a promising pathway to sustainable energy, with the potential for carbon-negative emissions under favorable feedstock and system-boundary conditions. Yet, the limitations of natural biological systems, such as poor energy conversion efficiency, huge carbon diversion, and poor operational robustness, have prevented its transition from laboratory research to industrial application. To resolve these bottlenecks, this review proposes a strategic shift from traditional biological conversion toward intelligent biomanufacturing via three enabling technologies: (1) synthetic biology to design microbial cell factories with a tailored hydrogen-centric metabolism; (2) nanomaterials engineering to create smart biotic-abiotic interfaces for overcoming the physical limitations of electron and mass transfer; and (3) artificial intelligence to enable autonomous bioprocessing through predictive digital twins and self-optimizing reactor systems. These three pillars can bridge molecular-scale engineering to system-level intelligence. A scalable roadmap starting from modular bioreactor design, waste-derived feedstock integration, and rigorous techno-economic and life-cycle assessment has been outlined to position biohydrogen within circular economy and potentially carbon-negative ecosystems. This review suggests a pathway to make biohydrogen an important, efficient, cost-effective, and reliable building block of the future hydrogen economy.

title: Passive anti-frosting strategies based on interfacial humidity regulation: From mechanisms to applications
abstract: Frost formation in low-temperature environments causes significant efficiency losses and safety hazards across aerospace, HVAC, and manufacturing industries. Conventional active anti-frosting methods suffer from poor energy efficiency due to periodic energy input requirements. This review summarizes recent advances in passive anti-frosting through interfacial humidity regulation—a strategy that inhibits ice crystal nucleation and growth by actively controlling local water vapor, offering substantial energy-saving potential. We firstly discuss theoretical models of ice nucleation in supersaturated vapor, examining how surface energy, microstructure, and chemistry govern interfacial humidity distribution and phase transitions. Secondly, three widely reported humidity regulating media, ice, hygroscopic gels, and hygroscopic liquids, are examined in terms of their vapor regulation mechanisms and frost suppression performance. Thirdly, we address advanced anti-frosting strategies based on interfacial humidity regulation via hygroscopic materials, biological protein and inspired microstructured surfaces. This review provides theoretical foundations and technical guidance for next-generation energy-efficient frost suppression technologies.

title: Self-regenerating photocatalytic water treatment systems: integrating cognitive AI control, bio-inspired self-healing, and thermoelectric energy harvesting
A probability-box framework for quantifying office building air conditioning flexibility under multi-source uncertainty
Dual-time-scale predictive hierarchical electro-thermal coordination for thermal-load reshaping in heavy-duty electric-drive hybrid vehicles
Bridging deterministic and stochastic scheduling: Learning risk-aware forecast adjustments for PV-BESS operation
Theory-guided lightweight decomposition for efficient and robust day-ahead electrical load forecasting
Catalysts or constraints? The dual role of natural resources and greenfield investment amid geopolitical risk
abstract: Rapid urbanisation, industrialisation, population growth, and fast economic expansion have made emerging economies significant contributors to greenhouse gas emissions. This study assesses the impact of key economic and environmental factors on economic development, emphasising the role of green growth as an effective means to achieve sustainable development. Specifically, it examines the effect of greenfield investment (GFI), geopolitical risk (GPR), natural resources (TNR), and renewable energy consumption (GET) on green growth (GG) across 17 emerging economies from 2003 to 2022. Utilising advanced panel estimation techniques, the study concludes that GFI and GET contribute positively to green growth, whereas GPR adversely affects green growth. Similarly, the greater dependence on natural resources significantly hampers green growth, thereby confirming the presence of the ‘resource curse’ hypothesis in our analysis. Moreover, the interaction between GPR and TNR significantly dampens green growth, while the interaction between GPR and GFI further exacerbates this adverse effect. Based on these results, the study suggests that policymakers should promote greenfield investment in sustainable sectors, strengthen natural resource management through robust regulations, and mitigate geopolitical risk by diversifying international partnerships to support long-term sustainable development goals.

title: Downside-risk pre-positioning for resilient scheduling of an off-grid deep-offshore electricity-hydrogen integrated energy system under extreme weather
A methodology for long-term hourly electricity demand forecasting driven by GDP and invariant load profiles
Variational Bayes-based multiple neural network method for battery SOC estimation
Transport characteristics and formation mechanism of voltage inconsistency in 200-cell PEMFC stack: Numerical reconstruction and experimental investigation
Environmental performance of energy consuming port activities based on a life cycle assessment
abstract: Fossil fuels are the primary energy source for logistical, energy intensive port operations, while being a major contributor to climate change, necessitating transition towards renewable and low emission energy sources. The issue is relevant given the expected growth in international maritime trade, resulting in increased port activities. This study uses life cycle assessment (LCA) to assess emission reduction potential in a Nordic container and cargo port when hydrotreated vegetable oil (HVO) and/or electricity is used instead of fossil fuels to power transportation, cargo handling equipment (CHE) and hoteling container vessels in the port. Additionally, the impact of replacing grid electricity and natural gas with on-site solar power (complemented with wind power from the grid) and biomethane in the port area is assessed. The novelty of the study lies in its comprehensive inclusion of port activities in the Nordic context and also includes CHE fleet production. Powering transportation and CHE fleet with HVO or grid electricity reduces port climate change impact (excluding biogenic emissions) nearly 60%. On-site photovoltaics and biomethane production, complementing needed electricity with wind power, and powering transport and cargo handling with HVO and electricity can result up to 78% reduction. Electrification demonstrated lower impacts compared to HVO scenario for climate change (incl. biogenic emissions), fine PM formation and terrestrial acidification impact categories. However, HVO outperforms electrification in eutrophication due to differences in equipment production. The findings indicate that electrification and HVO use enable significant emission reductions in the port and can be complemented by on-site energy production.

title: An Atomic-Scale Chemical Switch for Oxide Ferroelectricity
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Interfacial chemistry offers new opportunities for designing ferroelectric materials, yet their coupling with intrinsic polarization remains largely unexplored. Here, we synthesize ferroelectric BiFeO3 nanoparticles with {100} facets covered by a Bi2FeO6-x Aurivillius-like phase, allowing the interfacial Bi2O2 layer to interact with bulk polarization at different relative orientations. Using atomic-resolution scanning transmission electron microscopy, we observed a large polarization enhancement when the interface aligned with the bulk polarization, and a polarization reversal when opposing it. In situ heating and first-principles calculations show that the Bi2O2 layer repels the underlying FeO6 octahedra, which either rotate or rigidly displace to accommodate the chemical stress, depending on local geometry. Moreover, this mechanism can imprint local polarization in Aurivillius phases and nonferroelectric oxides, offering a general route to design polar topologies in oxide heterostructures.

title: Size effect on thermal runaway propagation in lithium-ion batteries: quantitative impact of size factor and suppression strategy
abstract: The continuous increase in the size of lithium-ion batteries significantly elevates the risk of thermal runaway propagation (TRP). Existing research has predominantly focused on specific, fixed cell formats, leaving both the mechanistic understanding of size effects on TRP incomplete and empirical mitigation strategies lacking cross-format scalability. Through combined experimental and modeling approaches, we systematically investigate the influence of battery size on TRP evolution characteristics. Furthermore, a system-level design response surface mapping the size factor ( F ) against the critical thermal insulation thickness is proposed. The results demonstrate a clear positive correlation between the F and the peak heat transfer power during TRP. Relying solely on adjusting the battery size proves insufficient for effectively inhibiting the TRP of Li(Ni x Co y Mn z )O 2 (NCM) batteries. This quantitative framework minimizes development trial-and-error costs by guiding the geometric optimization of large-capacity single cells and the a priori thermal sizing for system design.

title: Transport-interface coupling regulates calendar aging in lithium metal batteries
abstract: Lithium metal batteries (LMBs) are promising next-generation energy storage systems, yet their practical deployment is severely hindered by rapid capacity loss during long-term storage, known as calendar aging. This degradation is commonly attributed to the chemical instability of the solid electrolyte interphase (SEI), while the role of electrolyte transport remains largely overlooked. Here, using a model Cl − /NO 3 − -containing electrolyte system with systematically varied glyme chain length (G2-G4), we demonstrate that both SEI chemistry and electrolyte transport properties synergistically influence interfacial stability under static conditions. Shorter glyme chains promote the formation of an SEI enriched in Li 2 O and LiF, whereas longer chains yield a less protective SEI. Meanwhile, increasing solvent chain length progressively deteriorates ionic transport and interfacial kinetics. These combined effects lead to heterogeneous lithium (Li) deposition and porous interfacial structures in electrolytes with longer glyme chains. Under static storage, the less protective SEI together with transport-limited interfacial heterogeneity synergistically accelerates micro-galvanic corrosion, Li loss, and calendar capacity decay, while the SEI with higher Li 2 O/LiF content and favorable transport properties effectively suppresses corrosion. By quantitatively correlating electrolyte transport properties, SEI composition, deposition morphology, corrosion kinetics, and full-cell performance, this work establishes that both the chemical nature of the SEI and the transport capability of the electrolyte are critical design parameters for achieving stable cycling and extended calendar life in LMBs.

title: More-efficient water splitting utilizing heated-cooled active pure water with reduced hydrogen bonds
abstract: Within the realm of renewable energy technologies—particularly those centered on hydrogen evolution reactions (HERs) and oxygen evolution reactions (OERs)—noble metals have long been regarded as the archetypal catalytic materials. In recent years, however, research efforts have pivoted toward earth-abundant, cost-effective catalysts featuring diverse compositional and structural motifs. A seminal development occurred in 2014 with the introduction of plasmon-activated water (PAW), an innovative system engineered through hot electron transfer (HET) from gold nanoparticles (AuNPs). In this review based on our published papers, we put forward an alternative paradigm aimed at enhancing HER and OER efficiencies by redirecting the focus onto water itself—specifically, a condensed water derived from Au-free processing of heated PAW containing trace amounts of Au. Relative to active PAW, this condensed form exhibits a diminished electron-doping character alongside more-pronounced disruption of hydrogen-bonding networks. Notably, its emergent properties are critically governed by the heating rate applied during PAW boiling. Analogous behaviors were observed in cooled active water, where the cooling rate during post-boiling treatment of deionized water (DIW) played a similarly decisive role. Remarkably, when employed in HER and OER applications, the heated-cooled active pure water—whether derived from PAW or DIW—consistently outperformed pristine DIW, a fact attributable to its distinctive features: reduced hydrogen-bond connectivity and a modified electron-doping state. Moreover, the latter property conferred upon the prepared active water a pronounced capacity for scavenging 2,2-diphenyl-1-picrylhydrazyl (DPPH) free radicals. Even after several days of aging, both the unique physicochemical characteristics and the corresponding electrochemical activities showed only marginal attenuation, underscoring its viability for real-world deployment. Collectively, our findings establish this stable active water as a promising green solvent platform capable of enabling more-efficient HERs and OERs in electrochemical systems.

title: Unlocking the green power of the North Sea: Identifying key energy infrastructure synergies for 2030 and 2040
abstract: The North Sea will play a key role in providing clean and secure energy for Europe. This not only requires the development of new offshore wind farms, but also their successful integration into the onshore system. In this work we analyze and compare three key integration options and their preferred siting (onshore vs. offshore): grid expansions, electricity storage, and the production, storage and transport of low-carbon hydrogen. We focus on their potential to reduce emissions and energy system costs – individually and in combination with each other. Additionally, we study the consequences of constraints on their implementation. We analyze the years 2030 and 2040, starting from the projections of installed energy infrastructure and demand from the Ten Year Network Development Plan (TYNDP) 2022 of the European Network of Transmission System Operators (ENTSO-E). Results show that cross-border electricity grid expansions across the North Sea are a no-regret measure, resulting in significant reductions in system costs and emissions compared to national grid expansions. By comparison, the production, storage and transport of hydrogen have a lower cost and emission reduction potential. In both the short and long term (2030 and 2040), electricity storage can help to reduce emissions, but it is not cost competitive unless emission reduction targets are enforced. Combining the three integration measures at optimal capacities provides additional benefits. Overall, the highest emission reductions can be achieved by combining electricity storage with an expansion of the grid, while the highest economic benefits can be achieved with a combination of grid expansions and hydrogen production for direct use in industry.

title: A comprehensive review on accurate numerical simulation of proton exchange membrane fuel cell
abstract: PEMFCs involve strongly coupled electrochemical reactions and transport processes of gas, water, charge, and heat. Numerical simulation is therefore an important tool for understanding internal transport phenomena, predicting performance, and supporting PEMFC design and operation. This structured narrative review synthesizes representative PEMFC numerical-simulation studies identified primarily through topic-specific manual searches of the Web of Science database. While many earlier reviews focus on individual processes, components, scales, or modeling routes, the present review connects numerical models from the MEA to macro-scale and multi-scale single-cell models, stack models, operational-process models, system temperature-control models, and efficient-study models based on artificial intelligence and similarity theory. The principal modeling approaches are compared in terms of their physical descriptions, applicable scales, computational costs, validation approaches, and suitable applications. The review shows multi-physics and multiscale models are essential for resolving coupled internal processes, but their effectiveness is constrained by uncertain transport and kinetic parameters, coupling methodology between scales, limited validation data for local physical fields, and high computational cost for large stacks. AI-assisted and reduced-order approaches can improve computational efficiency, but their prediction capability and applicable scale require further development. The review provides a structured summary and outlooks for selecting and improving PEMFC numerical models.

title: A comprehensive review of machine learning in proton-exchange membrane fuel cells: From materials to intelligent systems
abstract: Machine learning (ML) is rapidly transforming proton-exchange membrane fuel cell (PEMFC) science by enabling advances across materials design, multiscale modeling, diagnostics, and intelligent control. Persistent barriers to widespread PEMFC deployment—including high cost, limited durability, and complex multiscale transport phenomena—arise from nonlinear interactions that conventional modeling and experimentation struggle to resolve. This review presents a comprehensive synthesis of ML approaches tailored to the PEMFC value chain, showing how numerical, experimental, imaging, and hybrid datasets support surrogate models that reduce Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD) computational costs by orders of magnitude while maintaining physical consistency through physics-informed and multi-fidelity learning. ML-guided optimization accelerates the rational design of catalyst layers, membranes, gas-diffusion media, and bipolar plates, uncovering non-intuitive structure–property relationships. Deep-learning-based diagnostics and hybrid residual frameworks significantly improve fault detection, state-of-health estimation, and remaining-useful-life prediction. At the system scale, ML-enhanced model predictive control and deep reinforcement learning enable adaptive, autonomous operation under dynamic conditions, while emerging digital-twin architectures integrate physics-based solvers with real-time data assimilation to deliver predictive, self-correcting fuel-cell management. By unifying methodological advances, cross-scale opportunities, and critical challenges, this review establishes ML as a foundational enabler for the next generation of high-performance, durable, and economically viable PEMFC technologies.

title: Circular economy practices and clean energy transition performance: the moderating role of critical mineral circularity and policy stringency among EU energy-intensive firms
Computational design of water splitting electrocatalysts: From d-band center to machine learning descriptors
abstract: Electrochemical water splitting is critical for sustainable hydrogen production, yet its commercial viability is limited by the sluggish kinetics of the hydrogen and oxygen evolution reactions (HER and OER). Computational chemistry has accelerated catalyst discovery through predictive activity descriptors. However, early descriptors are predominantly single-valued and static, built upon idealized models that omit dynamic surface reconstruction, electrolyte effects, and the coupling between multiple reaction pathways. These oversimplifications impair their capacity to break intrinsic scaling relationships and capture operando conditions, which has motivated a paradigm shift toward multidimensional, time-resolved frameworks. This review tracks the evolution of descriptors, from conventional volcano plots to machine learning-driven dynamic descriptors, and elaborates on how modern approaches capture structural evolution under operating potentials, bypass scaling constraints, and align theoretical model systems with realistic solid-liquid interfaces. Finally, we discuss prospective research directions, highlighting the integration of high-precision dynamic modeling, multi-objective optimization (which balances activity, stability, and mass transport), and closed-loop automated platforms to facilitate the on-demand design of robust electrocatalysts for industrial applications.

title: Advances in self-reconstructing stainless-steel electrocatalysts for water splitting: surface activation, alloy engineering, stability, and DFT insights
abstract: Stainless steel (SS) is emerging as a promising, earth-abundant platform for replacing precious-metal and pure-Ni electrodes in water electrolysis. Yet, it is still often treated as inert hardware rather than an active catalyst. Under HER/OER conditions, however, the classical Cr-rich passive film on Fe-Cr-Ni alloy SS is driven beyond its stability window. It can reconstruct into porous, Ni/Fe-rich (oxy)hydroxide layers that provide genuine catalytic activity while remaining anchored to a robust metallic backbone. This review consolidates evidence on how such self-reconstruction can be intentionally controlled and engineered to convert commercial SS into efficient, durable electrodes for overall water splitting. We first summarize the evolution of SS from a structural material to a self-reconstructing electrocatalyst, and critically discuss surface-activation strategies, including electrochemical activation (potential cycling, anodization, and cathodization), thermal oxidation, and hydrothermal/corrosion-engineering routes that drive Cr depletion and Ni/Fe enrichment. We then introduce the Ni-Fe-Cr-X reservoir concept to bridge the gap between traditional corrosion science and modern electrocatalysis, rationalizing how bulk alloy composition and microstructure govern reconstruction behavior, secondary passivation, and stability across alkaline and chloride-containing environments. Emphasis is placed on long-term durability, including self-replenishing Ni-rich electrodes that operate at ampere-level current densities, and on the limited but growing density functional theory (DFT) literature that links passive-film chemistry and electronic structure to HER/OER mechanisms. Finally, we outline key research directions, including multi-scale operando characterization, composition-designed SS, and specific DFT/ML frameworks needed to move from empirical activation toward rational, mechanism-guided design of SS-based electrocatalysts.

title: Investment-operation co-optimization of layered electricity‑hydrogen-derivative delivery networks for large-scale offshore wind clusters
Coordinated planning and operation of SST-based DC data centers with tiered workload flexibility
abstract: The rapid growth of artificial intelligence (AI) workloads is making modern data centers increasingly energy-intensive and reliability-critical. This trend not only raises electricity expenditure but also amplifies the economic impact of power interruptions, motivating coordinated planning of power infrastructure and computing resources. Against this background, solid-state transformer (SST)-based DC supply architectures are emerging as a promising direction for next-generation data centers because they provide a controllable interface for integrating diverse energy and computing resources. Under this architectural setting, this paper proposes a coordinated planning and operation framework for SST-based DC data centers with tiered workload flexibility. The framework incorporates nonlinear SST losses into long-term capacity planning, treats tiered workload flexibility as a planning resource, and coordinates energy storage and diesel generators for backup supply during utility outages. An annual bi-level model is formulated to jointly determine the capacities of SST conversion stages, renewable generation, energy storage, diesel generators, and heterogeneous computing servers, together with their scenario-dependent operating decisions. Piecewise linear approximation is used to reformulate the SST loss model, and an enhanced Benders decomposition algorithm is developed to solve the resulting multi-scenario mixed-integer problem. Case study results demonstrate that the proposed framework reduces total annual cost while satisfying workload service constraints. Further analysis shows that nonlinear SST losses influence capacity configuration, whereas tiered workload flexibility reshapes server deployment and backup resource requirements.

title: Impact of sub-hourly wind dynamics on green hydrogen yield and electrolyser lifetime
abstract: Direct wind-to-hydrogen systems, in which a wind farm supplies power to an electrolyser without a firm grid connection, must accommodate the full variability of the wind resource, yet many existing techno-economic and design studies rely on input data with temporal resolutions of several minutes to one hour. This coarse averaging can mask short-term power fluctuations that drive electrolyser performance, cycling and degradation. This paper presents a novel wind-to-electrolyser model that synthesises effective wind speed suitable for a power curve wind model at 1 Hz, combining low-frequency trend variation, mesoscale wind speed changes and Kaimal turbulence, validated against aeroelastic simulations. The resulting power output is supplied to a PEM electrolyser model incorporating bank-level thermal dynamics and steady-state, cyclic and on/off degradation, enabling the effect of wind-power variability on long-term electrolyser performance to be quantified. Using 10-year simulations of a wind farm at a site in Orkney, Scotland, two scenarios are investigated: the effect of wind farm size (1–10 turbines) and input temporal resolution (1 s, 1 min, 10 min) on power variability, degradation and hydrogen production; and the effect of turbine configuration for a fixed installed capacity (three 5 MW turbines versus one 15 MW turbine). Results show that coarser temporal resolution substantially overestimates hydrogen production, particularly for small wind farms, where 10-minute-averaged data increase predicted output by up to 428% relative to 1 s data, primarily due to underestimated on/off and cyclic degradation. Aggregating turbines and, to a lesser extent, using larger rotors both smooth the power input and reduce this sensitivity, though the effect remains significant even for 10-turbine farms. These findings demonstrate that high-frequency wind power variability must be explicitly considered in the design and performance assessment of wind-to-hydrogen systems.

title: Optimal design of pumped hydro compressed air energy storage considering air–water coupling characteristics
Fan Hong
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
